summary: This note is a documentation page for the UNDROP command, which restores a previously dropped object to the system. It gives the general syntax UNDROP <object_type> <identifier> and points to separate reference sections for Organization, Account and Database objects. It notes that not every DROP command has a corresponding UNDROP, and gives one example restoring a database named mydb.
one_line: Reference page for the UNDROP command, which restores dropped objects, with its syntax, usage note, and a database example.
key_facts: The UNDROP command restores the specified object to the system.
Reference sections are provided for Organization Objects, Account Objects, and Database Objects.
A general usage note states that not all DROP commands have a corresponding UNDROP.
The example UNDROP DATABASE mydb; restores a database named mydb.
The page's On this page section lists three headings: Syntax, General Usage Notes, and Examples.
